title.source: Section check: Trade, power and everyday lives
title.back: Section check: Trade, power and everyday life

intro.source: 6 questions about Lessons 4–6. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.back: 6 questions about Lessons 4–6. No need to hurry. You may look at the lessons again and try again as often as you like.
intro.note: Copied from the wording of Our World's Indonesian section checks.

questions.0.options.0.text.source: Many buyers try to buy the same spice.
questions.0.options.0.text.back: Many buyers try to buy the same spice.

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. When many buyers can compete, no one has a monopoly. Look back at Lesson 4.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. When many buyers can compete, nobody has a monopoly. Look at Lesson 4 again.

questions.0.options.1.text.source: One buyer shuts all the others out.
questions.0.options.1.text.back: One buyer pushes all the other buyers out.
questions.0.options.1.text.note: "Shuts all the others out" → "menyingkirkan semua pembeli lain" (pushes all the other buyers out), the verb Lesson 4 uses.

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. The VOC wanted to be the only buyer of Banda's nutmeg, so no one else could compete.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. The VOC wanted to be the only buyer of Banda's nutmeg, so that no other party could compete.

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Swapping goods is a kind of trade. A monopoly is when one group shuts other buyers or sellers out. Look back at Lesson 4.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Swapping goods is one kind of trade. A monopoly is when one group pushes other buyers or sellers out. Look at Lesson 4 again.

questions.1.question.source: The painting of Banda Neira cannot tell the whole story. Why not?
questions.1.question.back: The painting of Banda Neira cannot tell the whole story. Why not?

questions.1.options.0.text.source: It was made for the VOC, much later
questions.1.options.0.text.back: The painting was made for the VOC, much later

questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. The VOC paid for it more than 40 years after 1621. It shows the company's view, not what Bandanese people lived through.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. The VOC paid for it more than 40 years after 1621. The painting shows the company's point of view, not what Bandanese people went through.

questions.1.options.1.text.source: It was painted before nutmeg grew there
questions.1.options.1.text.back: The painting was made before nutmeg grew there

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Nutmeg grew on Banda for hundreds of years before the painting. It shows rows of nutmeg trees. Look back at Lesson 4.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Nutmeg had grown on Banda for hundreds of years before the painting was made. The painting shows rows of nutmeg trees. Look at Lesson 4 again.

questions.1.options.2.text.source: A painting can never be used as evidence
questions.1.options.2.text.back: A painting can never be used as evidence

questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The painting is useful evidence. It shows how the company chose to show Banda. It just cannot tell the whole story. Look back at Lesson 4.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The painting is useful evidence. The painting shows how that company chose to present Banda. The painting just cannot tell the whole story. Look at Lesson 4 again.

questions.2.question.source: Rubber went from a tree to a buyer far away. Which work did workers do on the way?
questions.2.question.back: Rubber moved from a tree to a faraway buyer. What work did the workers do on that journey?

questions.2.options.0.text.source: Buying shares in a rubber company
questions.2.options.0.text.back: Buying shares in a rubber company

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. An investor bought shares, hoping to get more money back. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. An investor bought shares, hoping to get more money back. Look at Lesson 5 again.

questions.2.options.1.text.source: Choosing photos for a souvenir book
questions.2.options.1.text.back: Choosing photos for a souvenir book

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The book's makers chose the photos. Workers tapped trees and collected and carried the rubber. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The book's makers chose its photos. The workers tapped the trees, then collected and carried the rubber. Look at Lesson 5 again.

questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. Workers tapped each tree and collected the latex. Others made it into sheets and took it to ships.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. The workers tapped each tree and collected its latex. Other workers processed it into sheets and took it to ships.

questions.3.stimulus.title.source: A made-up postcard from a made-up tea estate
questions.3.stimulus.title.back: A made-up postcard from a made-up tea estate

questions.3.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. A postcard from 1925 shows a tea estate on the made-up hill of Tavin. Rows of tea bushes cover the hill. Two workers pick leaves into baskets. A shop sold the postcard to visitors.
questions.3.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. A postcard from 1925 shows a tea estate on a made-up hill called Tavin. Rows of tea plants cover the hill. Two workers pick leaves into baskets. A shop sold the postcard to visitors.

questions.3.question.source: Which source could tell you what these workers were paid?
questions.3.question.back: Which source could tell you what these workers were paid?

questions.3.options.0.text.source: A bigger copy of the same postcard
questions.3.options.0.text.back: A copy of the same postcard in a bigger size
questions.3.options.0.text.note: "A bigger copy" → "salinan … dalam ukuran lebih besar", a little longer than the other options.

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. A bigger copy shows the same scene. A picture cannot show pay. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A bigger copy shows the same scene. A picture cannot show wages. Look at Lesson 5 again.

questions.3.options.1.text.source: A pay record from the estate
questions.3.options.1.text.back: A wage record from that estate

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. Pay is written in records, or told by the workers. A postcard shows only what its makers chose.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. Wages are written in records, or told by the workers. A postcard only shows what its maker chose.

questions.3.options.2.text.source: The number of baskets in the picture
questions.3.options.2.text.back: The number of baskets in the picture

questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The baskets show the work, not the pay. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The baskets show the work, not the wages. Look at Lesson 5 again.

questions.4.question.source: In 1903, Kartini and her sister were offered a scholarship. What happened next?
questions.4.question.back: In 1903, Kartini and her younger sister were offered a scholarship. What happened afterwards?
questions.4.question.note: "Her sister" (Roekmini) → "adiknya" (her younger sister), as in Lesson 6; "the sisters" → "kakak-beradik itu".

questions.4.options.0.text.source: The sisters did not use the money.
questions.4.options.0.text.back: The sisters did not use the money.

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. A decision shows what officials agreed to. It does not show what happened next. The sisters did not use the money.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. A decision shows what officials agreed to. The decision does not show what happened afterwards. The sisters did not use the money.

questions.4.options.1.text.source: Kartini used it to study in Batavia.
questions.4.options.1.text.back: Kartini used it to study in Batavia.

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The money was offered for study in Batavia. But the sisters did not use it. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The money was offered for study in Batavia. But the sisters did not use it. Look at Lesson 6 again.

questions.4.options.2.text.source: Kartini used it to open her school.
questions.4.options.2.text.back: Kartini used it to open her school.

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The school was a hope in her 1901 letter. The scholarship was a different thing, and it was not used. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The school was a hope in her 1901 letter. The scholarship was a different thing, and it was not used. Look at Lesson 6 again.

questions.5.question.source: You read Kartini's 1901 letter in an English book from 1921. Which question is good to ask about it?
questions.5.question.back: You read Kartini's 1901 letter in an English book from 1921. Which question is good to ask about that letter?

questions.5.options.0.text.source: Why did Kartini write it in English?
questions.5.options.0.text.back: Why did Kartini write it in English?

questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Kartini wrote mostly in Dutch. The English words are a translation. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Kartini wrote mostly in Dutch. The words in English are a translation. Look at Lesson 6 again.

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The letter is from 1901, and it tells us a hope. The decision is a different source. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The letter is from 1901, and it tells us a hope. The decision is a different source. Look at Lesson 6 again.

questions.5.options.2.text.source: Who chose and translated the letters?
questions.5.options.2.text.back: Who chose and translated those letters?

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. An editor chose which letters to print, and the book has only some of them. A translator made choices too.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. An editor chose which letters were printed, and the book contains only some of them. A translator also made choices.

results.high.source: Well done. You asked who made each source, and whose story it leaves out.
results.high.back: Very good. You asked who made each source, and whose story it does not tell.

results.middle.source: Good work. You got many questions right. Look back at the lessons for the ones you missed, and try again if you like.
results.middle.back: Good work. You answered many questions correctly. Look at the lessons again for the questions whose answers were not quite right, then try again if you want.
results.middle.note: Copied from Our World's Indonesian section checks.

results.low.source: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 4–6, then try again. You can take as long as you need.
results.low.back: Thank you for trying. Look at Lessons 4–6 again, then try again. You may take as much time as you need.
